messages:
alex_cs: Customer reported their function calls started failing after yesterday's canary. They say previously-valid JSON args now trigger schema validation errors.
alex_cs: Error they see: `400 Invalid function args` with body: \n```
{\n  \"error\": \"invalid_function_args\",\n  \"details\": \"Missing required field 'amount_cents'\"\n}\n```
alex_cs: Attaching the sample request they used and the system prompt they ship with the model.
alex_cs: Sample request payload they sent: \n```
{\"invoice_id\": \"inv_123\", \"amount\": 12.34, \"currency\": \"USD\"}
```
alex_cs: System prompt snippet from their integration: \n```
You are an helper that formats invoice tool calls. Always include human-friendly amounts (e.g., $12.34) and explanatory text. Prefer short descriptions.
```
alex_cs: They also added a few-shot example in the prompt that shows the function being called with `amount` as a human string like "$12.34".
devon_ml: I suspect the few-shot/system examples are overriding the model's tool output schema by nudging it to emit human strings instead of the numeric `amount_cents` field the tool expects.
maya_engineer: +1. We've seen this before: few-shot examples with formatted values cause the model to generate malformed args for strict JSON schemas.
maya_engineer: Can you paste the tool schema from their integration or the tool manifest? We need to confirm expected fields.
alex_cs: From the customer's tool manifest: \n```
name: create_invoice\nargs_schema: {\n  \"invoice_id\": \"string\",\n  \"amount_cents\": \"integer\",\n  \"currency\": \"string\"\n}
```
raj_infra: That mismatch explains the `Missing required field 'amount_cents'` — model produced `amount` (float) or `$12.34` string, not `amount_cents` integer.
devon_ml: Quick repro steps for engineering: ask the customer to run a call with the system prompt removed (or with a sanitized few-shot) and see if the toolcall succeeds. If it does, it's prompt-driven schema drift.
maya_engineer: For an immediate workaround recommend adding a pre-call validation/adapter on their side: convert `amount` or `$12.34` to `amount_cents` before forwarding to tool. Eg: parse `$12.34` -> 1234.
alex_cs: Customer asked if Redwood can block this on our side — they want an SLA fix. They're on Dedicated.
raj_infra: We shouldn't silently rewrite tool args on hosted/default path. For Dedicated we can propose an optional middleware: `llm-arg-normalizer` as part of deployment that runs schema normalization before tool invocation.
devon_ml: Long-term: we should add a warning in our docs and the Console: flag when system/few-shot examples contain fields that look like formatted values (dollar signs, commas) that conflict with tool arg schemas. Also an eval that checks for example->schema drift.
maya_engineer: Repro (I ran locally against same model snapshot): with system prompt + few-shot example the model emitted: \n```
{\"name\": \"create_invoice\", \"arguments\": {\n  \"invoice_id\": \"inv_999\",\n  \"amount\": \"$12.34\",\n  \"currency\": \"USD\"\n}}
```
maya_engineer: Without the few-shot/system example it emitted: \n```
{\"name\": \"create_invoice\", \"arguments\": {\n  \"invoice_id\": \"inv_999\",\n  \"amount_cents\": 1234,\n  \"currency\": \"USD\"\n}}
```
devon_ml: Policy note: for customers using function-calling we currently rely on the model to produce schema-compliant args. This shows examples can nudge it away. We should add a console alert: "prompt examples may override function arg formats".
alex_cs: Customer provided a request id: req_0a1b2c3d. They saw repeated failures since their last deploy (deploy-bot shows a canary at 2026-04-28 22:13 UTC).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished: service/customer-invoicer v1.14.3 -> 2026-04-28T22:13:12Z
alex_cs: Action items: 1) Ask customer to run one diagnostic call with sanitized prompt (I can provide curl). 2) Engineering to evaluate feasibility of arg-normalizer for Dedicated customers. 3) Docs/Console to add a warning and an eval test.
maya_engineer: I'll draft a minimal adapter and a unit test. If you share the customer's sample logs I'll reproduce and push a PR for the Dedicated middleware.
raj_infra: Also adding a quick runtime metric: count of failed function schemas per model per customer so we can surface regressions.
alex_cs: Thanks — I'll ask for the sanitized repro and share logs here when they respond. :thumbsup:
